tagline: The pipeline's haul road, all the way to the Arctic Ocean.
intro: The Dalton leaves the Elliott Highway north of Fairbanks and keeps the pipeline company for 414 miles to Deadhorse, near the Arctic Ocean. It was built as a haul road in 1974, 390 miles of it in five months, and opened all the way to the public only in 1994. Most of it is gravel.

It is the only road in the United States that crosses the Yukon River, the Arctic Circle and the Brooks Range. Along the whole length there are three towns, and the middle one, Wiseman, has a dozen people.
season: Alaska DOT&PF calls it best suited for travel June through August.

moments.title: Yukon River Bridge
moments.text: The only bridge over the Yukon in Alaska carries the highway and the pipeline together, built to change length by nearly two feet between summer and winter.

moments.title: Coldfoot
moments.text: Named, the story goes, for prospectors who got cold feet and turned back, it has a truck stop that began as hamburgers sold from a school bus, and no services north for 240 miles.

moments.title: Atigun Pass
moments.text: The road crosses the Continental Divide at 4,739 feet, the only pass in the Brooks Range a road goes over, with a turnout at the summit.

practical: Mostly gravel, with several steep grades. Fuel is sold at the Yukon River crossing, Coldfoot and Deadhorse; carry extra supplies and spare tires.
